title: Multipath Burst Fallback and Safety Recall — PRD (rough)
content:
Objective:
Short: Define a multipath burst/fallback mechanism for Dedicated pools that maximizes successful request completion during transient demand spikes while preserving tenant isolation and predictable billing.

Problem statement (why this exists):
- Dedicated pools occasionally face short high-amplitude demand spikes (microbursts) from a small set of tenants; existing soft-credit/burst models sometimes either: (a) allow noisy neighbors to consume headroom and cause SLO violations, or (b) over-throttle conservative tenants causing poor UX.
- When host-level pressure hits a threshold, we need a fast, deterministic strategy to: redirect, degrade, recall, or offload traffic with minimal human ops impact.
- Current fallback designs are single-path (fallback->hosted or fallback->lower-fidelity model). This creates a binary choice and unnecessary capacity stress.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Multipath burst routing: build a small routing fabric that can simultaneously attempt N fallback paths in prioritized order and accept earliest successful completion.
  - Example paths: local-dedicated-hotpool -> pooled-reserved-buffer -> hosted-fallback (lower-fidelity) -> queued-retry (client backoff).
- Safety recall token: introduce a short-lived recall token issued to a tenant when their burst is granted; token enables controlled recall/evacuation if pool pressure escalates.
- Bandwidth multipath shaping: limit per-tenant bandwidth across fallback paths to preserve fairness (soft caps + progressive throttling).
- Graceful evacuation handshake: define an operator and automated handshake for moving a tenant off a pool with minimal dropped requests and observability hooks.

Key user stories:
- As an SRE, I want the system to reroute 95% of affected requests to alternative paths with <150ms additional latency during a microburst without human intervention.
- As a customer, I want burst credits to be debited predictably and visible in console; I want to be able to opt into multipath fallback or lock to single-path.
- As product, I want metrics to indicate shards/paths attempted and success rates to tune economics.

Design details
1) Routing fabric and decision surface:
- Router decision inputs: tenant priority, current headroom per pool, recent tail latency, model compatibility (exact model version or compatible fallback), path cost estimate (tokens/latency).
- Router will issue parallel non-blocking attempts on multiple paths up to a configurable parallelism limit P (default P=2). First successful token wins; the rest are cancelled when possible.
- Cancellation semantics: best-effort cancellation of queued work on fallback pools; if cancellation fails, we track and attribute cost to originating tenant for reconciliation (billing rules).

2) Safety recall token (SRT):
- SRT is a GRPC-signed short token (TTL 30s) granted when tenant exhausts reserved headroom and is permitted to spill into alternate pool(s).
- Token semantics: grants temporary elevated routing permission but includes a recall bit. If pool pressure crosses critical threshold, recall is triggered and token holder is preemptively moved/fenced.
- Recall action sequence: (a) mark tenant as recall_pending in allocation table; (b) start handshake: send drain-notice (via control plane) to tenant's request router; (c) redirect new requests to alternate path; (d) allow in-flight requests to finish up to safe-timeout (default 5s); (e) if still active, forcibly revoke token and move to queued-retry.

3) Bandwidth/Concurrency shaping across paths:
- Global soft-share: configure soft max tokens/sec per tenant across multipath fabric; soft overcommit allowed with decaying credit.
- Progressive throttling: 3 bands: green (<= baseline reserved), amber (bursting with SRT), red (over-saturation -> immediate degradation to cheaper fallback or reject).
- Metrics to expose: tokens_used_by_path, concurrent_kv_cache_entries, avg_latency_by_path, recall_count_by_tenant.

4) Billing & Credit model:
- Billing attribution: primary path charges normally. If parallel attempts cause multi-path execution, charge first completion full price, secondary attempted but cancelled work is charged at discount (since compute wasted) and recorded as contested-burst-credit.
- Tenant-visible accounting: console shows SRT grants, contested charges (disputed), and a microburst summary.

5) Isolation & Fairness heuristics:
- Tenant weight normalization uses a combination of committed reservation, historical 24h p95 usage, and tenant SLAs.
- Noisy neighbor detection: sustained crossing of amber band > X% triggers auto-quarantine (soft eviction) with operator alert.

6) Canary and rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Simulation and backfill (run routing logic in dry-run mode, produce candidate decisions and compare to baseline). 2 weeks.
- Phase 1: Alpha on internal reserved pools with low-risk tenants. P=1 (no parallelization) for safety. 3 weeks.
- Phase 2: Beta for select customers with opt-in, P=2. Expose billing preview. 4 weeks.
- Phase 3: Gradual ramp to GA with opt-out and emergency kill-switch.

Operational runbook (ops-first notes)
- Detection:
  - Alert: pool_pressure > 85% for 30s AND recall_count > 0 -> P0
  - Alert: contested_burst_charges > threshold -> investigate router behaviour
- Immediate mitigation steps:
  1) Toggle multipath-default=off for affected region (console feature flag).
  2) Force drain tenant: set allocation.recall_forced=true (CLI: redwoodctl alloc recall --tenant $TENANT --force).
  3) If billing anomalies detected, run contested-charge reconciliation script (tools/recon/contested_charges.py).
- Postmortem checklist (if SLO breach): capture router logs for 2m window, snapshot KV cache sizes, collect path latencies, include tenant's request traces.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Parallelism P: higher P increases success probability but wastes compute and complicates billing. Need experiments to find diminishing returns curve.
- Cancellation guarantees: best-effort may still run expensive kernels; can we invoice at reduced rate or should we convert to tenant credit?
- Cross-region multipath: do we allow cross-region redirection as a fallback (costly egress + latency). Only for non-latency-sensitive endpoints?
- Operator surface: how granular should recall be (per-route vs per-tenant)? Default to per-tenant for simplicity; per-route could be future enhancement.

SLOs & metrics (proposed)
- Target: 95% of burst requests served within baseline latency + 200ms during microbursts (<=1min windows).
- Success metric: multipath_success_rate = completions_on_any_fallback / multipath_attempts.
- Economic guardrail: contested_charged_compute <= 2% of pool compute during steady state.

Implementation notes (engineering constraints):
- Router must be stateless-ish to scale; use short-lived allocation cache (ttl ~5s) populated from allocation service.
- Token signing: use existing KMS-based signing used for private deployments tokens.
- Backpressure: integrate with existing KV-cache and prefix cache cancellation hooks. If kernel is busy, we should prefer lighter-weight fallbacks (lower-fidelity quantized models) to reduce wasted GPU runtime.

Prototype checklist (engineers):
- [ ] Router shim that can attempt parallel GRPC calls to multiple endpoints and cancel via context cancellation.
- [ ] SRT issuance service with TTL and recall RPC.
- [ ] Billing hook to capture contested attempts and mark contested transactions.
- [ ] Console widget: microburst inspector showing recent multipath traces and contested charges.
- [ ] Run simulation on last 30 days of tenant traffic to estimate P curve and contested charge %, produce report.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally shaped as a pragmatic operational-first design rather than theoretical fairness optimization. We expect product + finance to weigh in on contested charge policy.
- Would like SRE / serving-runtime feedback on cancellation and kernel-level reclaim semantics — cc @Marco Li.

Quick links / snippets
- Example recall CLI: redwoodctl alloc recall --tenant acme-inc --timeout 5s --reason "safety_recall"
- Example SRT payload (Base64): eyJ0eXBlIjogIlNSVCIsICJ0bGwiOiAzMCwgInRlbmFudCI6ICJhY21lLWluYyJ9
